answer: Each identity posts a 500-unit bond locked for 30 epochs, anchored to one hardware credential, and that anchor cannot wander to another machine without registry re-signing. An attacker running N fake identities locks 500N units, forfeits 100 percent on detection, and waits 30 epochs before any refund. Splitting identities multiplies the marginal cost per fake while the shared registry mirror flags duplicate credentials, so a copying river of clones pays full bond each time and independent jurors slash all linked stakes.
